content.overview: The precautionary principle requires that lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing measures to prevent environmental degradation where there are threats of serious or irreversible damage. Sustainable development seeks to balance development with environmental protection so that present needs are met without compromising future generations. Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum recognised both principles as part of Indian environmental law.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Threat of serious or irreversible harm? (2) Scientific uncertainty — still act? (3) Development balanced with environment? (4) Distinguish from polluter pays?
content.study:
Precaution shifts the timing of regulatory action: authorities need not wait for conclusive proof of harm. Sustainable development is the balancing frame for project clearance and policy.

Cases already in migrated environment files (retained): Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996) 5 SCC 647. No new case invented.

sections.heading: Precautionary principle
sections.body: Where threats of serious or irreversible damage exist, lack of full scientific certainty is not a reason to postpone preventive measures.

sections.heading: Burden shift
sections.body: In application, the actor proposing a potentially harmful activity may be required to demonstrate environmental safety.

sections.heading: Sustainable development
sections.body: Development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

sections.heading: Vellore
sections.body: Precaution and polluter-pays are part of Indian environmental law and inform judicial and administrative action.

sections.heading: Forum
sections.body: NGT, High Court (Art. 226), Supreme Court (Arts. 32/136) as the cause and remedy allow.

examples.title: Uncertain risk project
examples.body: A project poses a credible threat of irreversible ecological harm; scientific data is incomplete — precaution supports preventive conditions or refusal pending adequate study.

hypotheticals.question: Must the regulator wait for conclusive proof before restricting a potentially harmful activity?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Under the precautionary principle, lack of full scientific certainty is not a reason to postpone measures against serious or irreversible threats.

distinctions.title: Precaution vs polluter pays
distinctions.left: Act early despite uncertainty to prevent harm.
distinctions.right: Allocate cost of harm and remediation to the polluter.

rows.right: After harm or for ongoing cost.

misconceptions.trap: Precaution means every project must be refused.
misconceptions.correction: Precaution requires preventive measures proportionate to the threat; it does not automatically equal prohibition.

cases.name: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: The precautionary principle and polluter-pays principle are part of Indian environmental law and must inform judicial and administrative action.
cases.holding: Directed remediation and compliance with environmental principles.
cases.relevance: Lead authority recognising precaution in India.
